column1: Process, procurement and contract management matter. They are not enough. Commissioners also need to understand whole systems, convene people around outcomes, work with citizens and providers, create room for experiment, and turn insight into practical action.
column2: A contract sets out what an organisation will buy. Participants examine what else shapes the result for the people using a service, including what partners do and which decisions citizens can influence.

column1: See the practice, not only the process

column1: A commissioning system can look orderly on paper while relationships, information, incentives, decision rights and capacity pull in different directions. The health check creates a usable picture of those conditions.

column1: It is not an inspection, benchmark or maturity score. It is a grounded diagnostic and a senior conversation about what the system is producing and what can sensibly change.
